sections.title: Introduction to Message Queues 📬
content: AMPS includes high performance queuing built on the AMPS messaging engine and the transaction log.
Unlike Basic Pub/Sub (where every subscriber receives a copy), AMPS Queues ensure that each message is processed by exactly one subscriber.
This is essential for task distribution, compute grids, and reliable order processing.

sections.title: Queue Models and Concepts 🎯
content: Point-to-Point: A message is sent from a publisher and delivered to a single consumer.
Competitive Consumption: Multiple workers subscribe to the same queue. AMPS distributes messages among them based on availability and capacity.
Single Consumer: A specific configuration where only one consumer can be active at a time, often used for strict ordering.

sections.title: Queue Configuration & Semantics ⚙️
content: Lease Period: The time a consumer has to process a message. If not acknowledged (via sow_delete) within this window, AMPS returns it to the queue.
At-Least-Once Delivery: The standard AMPS guarantee ensuring messages are redelivered if a consumer fails.
Max Deliveries: Limits the number of times a message can be retried before being removed or moved to a dead-letter queue.
Expiration: The 'Time to Live' (TTL) for a message in the queue.

sections.title: Delivery Strategies ⚖️
content: Round Robin: Messages are delivered sequentially to available consumers.
Proportional: Messages are distributed based on the declared capacity (max_backlog) of each consumer.
Least Loaded: AMPS prioritizes consumers with the most available capacity.

sections.title: Distributed Queues 🌐
content: AMPS allows queues to work across replicated instances while maintaining 'once-and-only-once' delivery guarantees.
Replicated instances coordinate ownership to ensure that even in a distributed environment, consumers don't double-process the same message.
This allows for global scale and high availability in message processing workflows.
